summary: Extended the measured coverage of the accepted-then-panicking configuration change from one explicit transition value to both. Since EnterJoint treats JointImplicit as a joint transition just like JointExplicit, the same empty change set with JointImplicit is accepted by propose-time validation and then panics on apply; the extended harness (now three cases: explicit, implicit and the Auto control over the same joint configuration) confirms locally that for the implicit form leave_joint is false, enter_joint_ok true, the proposal step returns no error and leaves an EntryConfChangeV2, and applyConfChange panics with config is already joint while still joint, whereas the Auto control leaves the joint configuration with no panic. Submitted as a successor experiment for the same investigation with two implicit-case comparisons (last_type EntryConfChangeV2, panicked true) plus scope, prefix, prerequisite and knowledge uses, so the controller can produce the receipt. This broadens the condition under which the already-recorded asserted defect is reachable - any non-Auto transition with zero changes in a joint configuration - and does not change the claim itself.
